evidence.alignment: The selected technologies (intravascular 3D imaging, surgical AI guidance, high-sensitivity diagnostic automation) align well with high-growth medical device markets, but the mean timing error of 1.83 years—especially the 3.25-year lag for T02 relative to its 2026-Q4 boom—indicates poor market timing awareness for the most strategically critical asset.
evidence.sequencing: Dependency chains are respected with zero violations: T01 completes at 2028-Q1 before T02 begins, satisfying the prerequisite. TRL levels (6-7) support the planned development windows, though T02's late start misses its market boom window significantly.
evidence.investment: T01 and T02 receiving Strategic tier investment is well-justified given their high market opportunity and urgency scores (5.0), while T03 at High tier appropriately reflects its lower strategic fit and market opportunity scores (3.0 each). The differentiation between tiers is rational and proportional.
evidence.coherence: The three technologies form a coherent clinical imaging and diagnostic progression—from vascular 3D imaging infrastructure, to AI-guided surgical application, to automated diagnostic systems—representing a logical research-to-deployment narrative in medical imaging.
evidence.balance: With only 3 technologies all clustered in TRL 6-7 (development/near-deployment stage), there is no early-stage research investment and limited portfolio diversity. Two technologies share the same 2028-Q1 start date, concentrating risk temporally, and there are no low-tier exploratory bets.

strengths: Zero dependency violations with T01 correctly sequenced as a prerequisite for T02, ensuring technical feasibility of the roadmap.
Investment tier differentiation between Strategic (T01, T02) and High (T03) is well-calibrated to the underlying scoring metrics for market opportunity and urgency.
weaknesses: T02 (Surgical AI Image Processing) is scheduled to complete in 2030-Q1, which is 3.25 years after its market boom in 2026-Q4, meaning the technology will arrive far too late to capture peak market value.

The portfolio lacks diversity in TRL stages and investment tiers—no exploratory or low-tier technologies are included, and all assets are concentrated in near-deployment phases with no long-horizon R&D bets.
missing_technologies: Early-stage AI/ML model development platform for medical imaging (TRL 3-4) to feed the pipeline beyond 2030
Robotic surgical assistance technology to complement surgical AI image guidance (T02)
Remote patient monitoring or digital health integration technology for post-surgical care continuity
investment_issues: Despite T02 having the highest market opportunity score (5.0), its Strategic tier investment cannot compensate for the fundamental timing problem of a 3.25-year delay past market boom—investment tier alone does not resolve schedule misalignment.
Budget utilization is reported as 0 spent against a 13.5B budget, suggesting investment allocation may be planned but not yet operationalized, raising execution risk.
timing_issues: T02 (수술용 AI 기반 이미지 처리 및 안내) targets completion in 2030-Q1 but its market boom peaks at 2026-Q4, resulting in a 3.25-year miss that renders the technology commercially late to its primary opportunity window.
T03 (고감도 진단 자동화 시스템) completes in 2030-Q1 against a 2028-Q2 boom, meaning it also arrives 1.75 years after peak market demand.
T01's 0.5-year overshoot past its 2027-Q3 boom is minor but still indicates the roadmap could be accelerated by one quarter to better capture peak demand.
